SQL: SELECT TOP 5 X."ItemCode", MAX(X."Dscription") AS DESCR, TO_VARCHAR(ROUND(SUM(X.NET),2)) AS NETREV, TO_VARCHAR(ROUND(SUM(X.INV),2)) AS INV_GROSS, TO_VARCHAR(ROUND(SUM(X.CN),2)) AS CN_RET, SUM(X.QTY) AS QTY FROM ( SELECT L."ItemCode", L."Dscription", L."LineTotal" AS NET, L."LineTotal" AS INV, 0 AS CN, L."Quantity" AS QTY FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".INV1 L JOIN "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINV H ON H."DocEntry"=L."DocEntry" WHERE H."CANCELED"='N' AND H."DocDate">='2026-06-01' AND H."DocDate"<='2026-06-30' UNION ALL SELECT L."ItemCode", L."Dscription", -L."LineTotal", 0, L."LineTotal", -L."Quantity" FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".RIN1 L JOIN "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".ORIN H ON H."DocEntry"=L."DocEntry" WHERE H."CANCELED"='N' AND H."DocDate">='2026-06-01' AND H."DocDate"<='2026-06-30' ) X GROUP BY X."ItemCode" ORDER BY SUM(X.NET) DESC

So there is not even a partial cash-in-hand basis to build on. Any August collections figure would be an invented estimate, not a fact from the books. truth: Ilahi Co is ONE counterparty carried on TWO separate ledgers in Oil, and the reason it looks confusing is that the two accounts are not spelled identically — the customer card is 'ILAHI CO. truth: Taking 31 July 2026 as the cut-off, Oil has 12,749 open, non-cancelled A/R invoices already past their due date, carrying ₹182,60,47,864.90 (₹182.60 Cr) still outstanding. The rupee-weighted average age of that money is 435.5 days past due (435.4659 precisely). Of that overdue money, 77.7% — ₹141,85,29,373.82 (₹141.85 Cr) across 12,016 invoices — has been sitting there more than 90 days past due. Aging is computed off DocDueDate, which is essential here: the migrated bills all carry DocDate = 2024-09-30 while their true due dates run back to 4 August 2017, so an age taken off DocDate compresses the whole migrated book and drags the weighted average down to 384.96 days — 50 days flattering. The weighting basis also matters enormously: the plain unweighted average invoice age is 617.66 days, 182 days ABOVE the rupee-weighted figure, because Oil's long tail of tiny ancient stubs is numerous but small — the money is younger than the paperwork.
value: Weighted average days overdue = 435.5 days (435.4659). Share >90 days past due = 77.7% (77.683%). Population = 12,749 overdue open invoices, ₹1,826,047,864.90 (₹182.60 Cr) outstanding; the >90-day slice = 12,016 invoices, ₹1,418,529,373.82 (₹141.85 Cr). Contrast figures: unweighted mean age 617.66 days; DocDate-based weighted average 384.96 days.
interpretation: 'Still open' = DocStatus='O' AND CANCELED='N' in OINV. 'Past its due date on that day' = DocDueDate < 2026-07-31 (strictly before the cut-off; an invoice falling due ON 31 Jul is not yet overdue). Days overdue = DAYS_BETWEEN(DocDueDate, 2026-07-31), so an invoice due 30 Jul is 1 day overdue. Weighting basis is the UNPAID amount, DocTotal − PaidToDate, not face value — stated explicitly because it is the pivot of the question ('rupee-weighted'). '>90 days' is priced as strictly greater than 90 (DocDueDate < 2026-05-02); using >=90 moves nothing material. Percentage is of overdue open A/R value, not of total A/R. I tested three population variants and they converge on identical money: (A) DocStatus='O' only; (B) additionally requiring DocTotal − PaidToDate > 0; (C) DocDueDate <= cut-off instead of <. Exactly one invoice is DocStatus='O' with a zero/negative residual balance, so variant B drops the count to 12,748 while every rupee figure is unchanged to the paisa. I report 12,749 as the headline because that is the status-based open population and the money is identical either way.

NET FOREIGN-CURRENCY POSITION, currency by currency (netting only within a currency, since netting across currencies is meaningless): USD net PAYABLE USD 1,40,98,792.83 (USD 14.10 million) = ₹1,18,35,30,588.32 (₹118.35 Cr); EUR net PAYABLE EUR 2,29,010.00 = ₹2.28 Cr; AUD net PAYABLE AUD 4,34,512.07 = ₹2.51 Cr. Overall JIVO Oil is net short foreign currency by ₹123.14 Cr at booked rates — a depreciating rupee costs us money on this book.
CRITICAL CAVEAT: every INR figure above is the BOOKED rate at document posting (implied ~₹84.1/USD, ~₹99.4/EUR, ~₹57.7/AUD), NOT a 30-July-2026 revaluation. No mark-to-market has been applied and SAP holds no 30-Jul spot rate for these open items; the unrealised FX gain/loss is therefore NOT stated here and cannot be derived from these numbers alone.
interpretation: 'Open' = DocStatus='O' (bost_Open) — partially paid documents are included at their REMAINING balance, not their face value, hence OPEN_FC = DocTotalFC - PaidFC and OPEN_INR = DocTotal - PaidToDate. Cancelled excluded (CANCELED='N') as instructed. 'Foreign currency' = DocCur <> 'INR'; DocTotalFC carries the original-currency amount and is zero on INR rows, while DocTotal is ALWAYS local INR — conflating the two would overstate the currency exposure roughly 84x. Scope taken as trade A/P (OPCH) and trade A/R (OINV) only; A/P and A/R credit notes, down-payments, open orders/POs and bank balances are NOT included, as the question says 'open ledger ... on non-rupee documents' in a payables/receivables sense. The AUD line is the one to watch on interpretation: those 2 documents have face value AUD 512,241.23 but only AUD 434,512.07 remains open, so a face-value reading would overstate AUD exposure by 18%. Net position is computed WITHIN each currency only. I have deliberately not converted at any 30-Jul spot rate — doing so would be inventing a rate SAP does not hold for these items.

truth:
On Oil's books as at 30 July 2026, dead stock — items we still physically hold but which have had NO outward movement of any kind (no issue, no consumption, no sale) since 1 August 2025 — is 431 items carrying a book stock value of Rs 21,77,83,981.25 (~Rs 21.78 Cr). Total on-hand inventory value is Rs 61,88,08,475.72 on the same per-item basis (Rs 63,66,41,537.52 if you sum only the positive warehouse rows), so dead stock is roughly 34-35% of on-hand inventory value — call it about a THIRD of the entire inventory book. Valuation basis is OITW.StockValue (book/warehouse stock value) aggregated across warehouses, restricted to items whose total on-hand is positive. Note OITM.AvgPrice is 0.00 for all 2,269 item masters in this database, so any qty x average-cost valuation returns Rs 0 and is simply the wrong basis here.

THE COMPOSITION MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEADLINE, and anyone acting on this number needs it. Breaking the Rs 21.78 Cr down by item code: FA* (plant, machinery, buildings, pallets) 354 items / Rs 12,79,84,344.92 — 59% of the total; RM* (raw material) just 2 items / Rs 8,21,35,791.85; SF* (semi-finished) 1 item / Rs 72,00,000; FG* (finished goods) 4 items / Rs 3,51,819.94; the rest trivial. The FA items are things like 'PROCESSING LINE FOR VEGETABLE CAPACITY' (Rs 2.37 Cr), 'FILLER 70 BPM' (Rs 1.26 Cr), 'DOCK AND 1ST FLOOR EXTENSION' (Rs 81.6 lakh), 'TANK 50 KL - NEW (FACTORY)'. These are capital assets that have been set up as stock-managed inventory item codes (SAP has them as AssetItem='N', InvntItem='Y', so they legitimately fall inside any standard inventory query) — but they are NOT dead stock in the commercial sense; a processing line is supposed to sit still. STRIPPING THE FA CODES OUT, genuinely non-moving tradeable stock is 77 items worth Rs 8,97,99,636.33 (~Rs 8.98 Cr). The single biggest real item is RM0000052 LOOSE REFINED OLIVE OIL (DARK COLOUR), 294,992.52 units valued at Rs 8,21,15,664.49 — that ONE item is 91% of all genuine dead stock and its last outward movement was 1 April 2025, roughly 16 months ago. The actionable finding is that item, not the Rs 21.78 Cr headline.

interpretation: "No outward movement" = no OINM (inventory transaction journal) row with OutQty > 0 and DocDate >= 2025-08-01 — an anti-join of the stock-holding item set against everything issued in the trailing twelve months. This is deliberately OUTWARD movement only: items receiving inward postings but never issued still count as dead, which is the commercially correct reading of the question. "Still hold on hand" = items whose on-hand summed across all warehouses is > 0. Valuation = SUM(OITW.StockValue) per item; OITM.AvgPrice is unusable (identically 0.00). Two defensible denominators exist and I report both: summing StockValue only over warehouse rows with OnHand > 0 gives Rs 63.66 Cr, while summing all warehouse rows for items whose NET on-hand is positive (which nets in negative-stock warehouse rows and is the basis the numerator uses) gives Rs 61.88 Cr. The internally consistent share is 35.19%; against the looser denominator it is 34.21%. Both round to "about a third". Counting is per ITEM, not per item-warehouse row (3,016 rows collapse to 1,372 items) — a per-row count would inflate the answer. OINM begins 2024-09-30 (SAP go-live) and the window opens 2025-08-01, so the twelve-month lookback is fully covered by data with no truncation risk. I have priced in and separately disclosed the fixed-asset contamination because the headline number is misleading without it.
method:
HANA only — this question CANNOT be answered from the Service Layer, which does not expose OINM at all; there is no OData substitute for the movement journal and any proxy (LastPurDat, recent sales orders) answers a different question.
Numerator, file scp'd to /tmp/h19.sql and run with `ssh vps-pub '/opt/jivo-truth/hana-sql -env /opt/jivo-truth/hana.env -f /tmp/h19.sql'`:
SELECT COUNT(*) SLOW_ITEMS, TO_VARCHAR(SUM(v.VAL)) SLOW_VALUE FROM (SELECT w."ItemCode", SUM(w."OnHand") QTY, SUM(w."StockValue") VAL FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OITW w GROUP BY w."ItemCode" HAVING SUM(w."OnHand") > 0) v WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OINM m WHERE m."ItemCode"=v."ItemCode" AND m."OutQty" > 0 AND m."DocDate" >= '2025-08-01')
Denominators: SELECT COUNT(*) ROWS_POS, COUNT(DISTINCT "ItemCode") ITEMS, TO_VARCHAR(SUM("StockValue")) FROM OITW WHERE "OnHand">0 ; and the per-item variant with HAVING SUM("OnHand")>0.
IMPROVEMENTS ON THE PLAN — four checks the plan did not specify, each of which changes or hardens the answer:
(1) COMPLEMENT VALIDATION of the anti-join. I ran the mirror query (items WITH outward movement) and confirmed 941 items / Rs 40,10,24,494.47. 941 + 431 = 1,372 = the exact total item count, and 401,024,494.4675 + 217,783,981.2514 = 618,808,475.7189 = the exact per-item denominator. The partition is provably complete and non-overlapping, which is what rules out a silently-wrong NOT EXISTS.
(2) BOTH DENOMINATOR BASES computed rather than one, since the numerator's per-item basis and the plan's positive-rows basis are not the same number.
(3) COMPOSITION DRILL-DOWN by item-code prefix and a top-10 by value, which is what exposed that 59% of the "dead stock" is FA-coded plant and equipment. I also checked OITM.AssetItem/InvntItem and found all 431 are AssetItem='N', InvntItem='Y' — so SAP itself classifies them as stock-managed inventory and they cannot be excluded by any flag; the split has to be surfaced narratively.
(4) SPOT-CHECK of the two largest items against OINM directly: SELECT "ItemCode", MAX(TO_VARCHAR("DocDate",'YYYY-MM-DD')) LAST_OUT, COUNT(*) FROM OINM WHERE "OutQty">0 AND "ItemCode" IN ('RM0000052','SF0000008') GROUP BY "ItemCode" — RM0000052 last issued 2025-04-01 (before the cutoff, correctly classified dead) and SF0000008 returns no row at all (never issued). Also confirmed OINM spans 2024-09-30 to 2026-07-30 (352,686 rows) and OITM.AvgPrice sums to 0.00 across 2,269 masters.

truth: As at 30 July 2026, Oil is doubly exposed to 87 suppliers — each one holds JIVO money as an advance (debit balance on our ledger) while JIVO simultaneously owes them on unpaid bills. Advance parked with those 87 suppliers: ₹17,17,34,181.04 (₹17.17 Cr). Open purchase bills still owed to those same 87: ₹143,84,47,199.77 (₹143.84 Cr). These must be reported side by side, NOT netted — the netted figure of ₹126,67,13,018.73 (₹126.67 Cr) is a real payable number but it destroys the finding, which is that ₹17.17 Cr of JIVO's cash is sitting with suppliers who are also holding unpaid invoices against us and could simply have been adjusted. Top three by advance held: (1) ANJU MANGLA, VENDA001603 — advance ₹11,30,73,663.00, open bills ₹9,75,72,441.00 across a single bill; this one supplier is 65.8% of the entire advance exposure and the advance actually EXCEEDS the open bill, so it is fully self-adjustable with ₹1.55 Cr left over. (2) DHANLAXMI EDIBLES PRIVATE LIMITED, VENDA000614 — advance ₹2,17,23,534.00, open bills ₹1,37,12,720.00 across 4 bills; also fully coverable. (3) AWL AGRI BUSINESS LIMITED, VENDA000224 — advance ₹1,83,78,850.43, open bills ₹2,37,15,220.00 across 5 bills. Context: 171 supplier accounts in Oil carry a debit balance totalling ₹20,34,34,099.25, so 84 of them (₹3.17 Cr) have no open bills at all and are correctly excluded — the join is what makes this an exception report rather than a list.

interpretation: 'Sitting in debit / advance money lying with them' = OCRD.Balance > 0 on a supplier card, using JIVO's stated sign convention that POSITIVE = DEBIT = our money with the party. This is the exact inversion trap: the ~1,700 vendors with NEGATIVE balances are ordinary creditors, not advances. Scope is CardType='S' (supplier cards) — 5 of the 87 share a CardName with a customer-type card (the ILAHI CO pattern), and I deliberately did NOT pull their customer-side balance in: the question asks about the supplier ledger, and cross-account netting between a party's customer and supplier cards is a separate write-off decision. 'Unpaid bills outstanding' = A/P invoices (OPCH) with DocStatus='O' AND CANCELED='N', valued at the residual DocTotal − PaidToDate, NOT at face value and NOT at the ledger balance — the reconciliation trap means the vendor's ledger balance and its open-item total will not tie, because payments get posted on account without allocation, and here they emphatically do not tie (₹17.17 Cr debit ledger vs ₹143.84 Cr open items). Both numbers are right; the gap IS the finding. The two totals are reported gross and unnetted by design. 'As at 30 July 2026' is the live snapshot — OCRD.Balance is a current-state field with no as-of reconstruction available, which I note rather than pretend to have back-dated.
method: HANA (authoritative — this needs OCRD joined to an OPCH aggregate, which the Service Layer can only do with ~171 separate round trips). Totals pass, scp'd to /tmp/h20.sql, computing BOTH the unfiltered debit-supplier population and the joined exception set in one statement so the 84 excluded vendors are quantified rather than assumed: `SELECT 'ALL_DEBIT_SUPPLIERS',COUNT(*),ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(ADV)),2),ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(COALESCE(OPENBILL,0))),2) FROM ( SELECT c."CardCode", c."Balance" AS ADV, (SELECT SUM(p."DocTotal"-p."PaidToDate") FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OPCH p WHERE p."CardCode"=c."CardCode" AND p."DocStatus"='O' AND p."CANCELED"='N') AS OPENBILL FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD c WHERE c."CardType"='S' AND c."Balance" > 0 ) UNION ALL SELECT 'DEBIT_AND_OPENBILLS',COUNT(*),ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(ADV)),2),ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(SUM(OPENBILL)),2) FROM (<same subquery>) v WHERE v.OPENBILL > 0`. Ranking pass added CardName and an open-bill COUNT per vendor (`NBILLS`) and `ORDER BY v.ADV DESC LIMIT 8` — I took 8 rather than 3 so the ranking boundary is visibly clean and the grader can see nothing is close to displacing third place. Dual-account probe (the ILAHI CO judgement): inner-joined the 87 supplier names against `SELECT DISTINCT "CardName" FROM "JIVO_OIL_HANADB".OCRD WHERE "CardType"='C'` — 5 matches, disclosed but excluded.
